hypothesis: The default locking provider is in-memory, so the lock that serializes the availability check and reservation write in reserveInventoryStep only lives inside one Medusa process. With two servers on one database, two completions of carts that each need the single SOLO unit can run on different servers at the same time, both pass the available_quantity check, and both create reservations, so live reservations exceed stock (no_oversell fails). I expect this to show up when the two completions are released together, since their reservation writes can interleave across processes.

hypothesis: reserveInventoryStep locks only on inventory item ids and runs createReservationItems, which reads available_quantity and then writes reservations. Within one server this lock should serialize calls, so I expect no oversell on a single server.
